conclusion.headline: Only Conv1 legacy Adam is core-bracketed; no Conv1 learning rate is frozen.
conclusion.observation: All six Conv1 surfaces produced a passing diagnostic core candidate between 94.46% and 96.18% final validation accuracy. Five surfaces have a passing 2% loss plateau on an upper rho boundary; legacy Adam is the only core-bracketed surface. Only baseline SGD was published before the selector failed, so the other five decisions are read-only reconstructions.
conclusion.interpretation: The core measurements show that the diagnostic optimizer setup can train every Conv1 surface above the 90% gate. They do not establish a cross-scheme or cross-optimizer winner. The user-fixed gain 40 and T/K 4/4 are ordinary-MNIST diagnostic inputs, and the incomplete selector prevents a frozen learning-rate handoff.
conclusion.decision: Keep the complete core evidence as a reviewed diagnostic. Freeze no Conv1 learning rate and do not treat 96.18% as final-paper accuracy. Conv1 expansion remains outside the currently requested next batch.
limitations: Ordinary MNIST rather than deterministic medium affine MNIST.
Three-epoch optimizer screen rather than authorized final training.
Five of six selector decisions are read-only reconstructions.
Five surfaces remain on a search boundary.
The official test set was not read.

claims.statement: The Conv1 shard contains a hash-verified completion chain for all 53 promoted core candidates.
Read-only application of the intended selector brackets the Conv1 legacy-Adam core surface at rho_conv=0.003 and rho_dense=0.01.
Legacy Adam has the highest observed Conv1 core validation accuracy at 96.18%, but this is not a general optimizer or scheme comparison.
This incomplete ordinary-MNIST core screen does not freeze a Conv1 learning rate or support a final-paper accuracy claim.
